newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-LEICESTER PULL PLUG ON BATH DOMINANCE. [CORRECTED 16:15 GMT]
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-LEICESTER PULL PLUG ON BATH DOMINANCE. [CORRECTED 16:15 GMT]

text.p: Bath's stranglehold on English domestic rugby was further weakened on Saturday when they lost 39-28 at home to Leicester in the Pilkington Cup sixth round.

England A centre Will Greenwood, playing opposite national captain Phil de Glanville and Jeremy Guscott, scored two tries and made a superb third for winger Steve Hackney to end Bath's hopes of a fourth (corrects from "third") successive Cup triumph.

Bath have won the competition 10 times in the last 13 years (corrects from "nine times in the last 12 years") but were well beaten by a Leicester side who bounced back superbly from their European Cup final disappointment against France's Brive last month.
They scored five tries in all and South Africa's World Cup fly-half Joel Stransky contributed 14 points in his first showpiece game in English rugby.
"We got a real stuffing against Brive so we had a lot to prove today," said Greenwood."The commitment and the tackling were superb and it's nice to have Joel at stand-off to cool things down."
Leicester now face Rob Andrew's Newcastle in the quarter-finals in two weeks time.
